claims.text: UA and USU imaging for sus renal colic; once a stone = confirmed, look for the cause, incl stone composition.
claims.quote: Patients suspected of having a calculus causing colic require urinalysis and usually an imaging study. If a calculus is confirmed, evaluation of the underlying disorder, including calculus composition testing, is required.

claims.text: UA: hematuria = common but urine can be norm; pyuria suggests infect.
claims.quote: Macroscopic or microscopic hematuria is common, but urine may be normal despite having multiple calculi. Pyuria with or without bacteria may be present. Pyuria suggests infection

claims.text: Noncontrast CT = the preferred first study: stone location, degree of obstruct, and other Eti such as aortic aneurysm.
claims.quote: Noncontrast CT is the preferred initial imaging study in most patients. This study can detect the location of a calculus as well as the degree of obstruction. Moreover, CT may also reveal other causes of the pain (eg, aortic aneurysm).

claims.text: US or abd XR can confirm a stone w little or ⍉radiation in typical cases.
claims.quote: For patients with typical symptoms, ultrasonography or abdominal radiographs can usually confirm presence of a calculus with minimal or no radiation exposure.

claims.text: Consider a dissecting aortic aneurysm, esp in older pts.
claims.quote: Dissecting aortic aneurysm must be considered, particularly in older patients
